cohort: Pregnant women who delivered after 38 weeks of gestation at Hospital Estadual Azevedo Lima (HEAL), Niteroi, Brazil, during a three-month period
finding: Emergency cesarean section was associated with the worst perinatal outcome, with a significantly higher rate of NICU admission compared to vaginal delivery and elective cesarean section.
mod_finding: Neonatal intensive care unit admission rates were significantly higher for infants delivered by emergency cesarean section during labor compared to those delivered vaginally.
